frequency_question: How often does structural friction prevent a central bank from implementing a widely anticipated or economically warranted rate hike during a tightening cycle?
membership_rule: Includes all scheduled rate-setting meetings during identified emerging market monetary tightening cycles where inflation metrics exceeded target bounds; excludes emergency inter-meeting moves and non-tightening cycles.
coverage_note: 7 named meetings covering the most recent complete domestic tightening cycle; representative of institutional friction frequency.
known_gaps: Does not capture informal ministerial pressure behind closed doors, only formal committee divergence and procedural friction.
skeleton: RBI monetary policy committee meetings during recent tightening cycles where external structural friction (e.g., dissenting votes, liquidity floors, government deficit pressures) tested the committee's resolve.
multiplier: 1 successful friction block out of 7 major tightening decisions
validity_reason: Central bank institutional frameworks, statutory inflation-targeting mandates, and voting structures remain stable across multi-year appointments.
